plan: starting-weights experiment, part 2: CNN arm and replication on the EyePACS confirmation set
written: 2026-09-25, before the ResNet50 models are trained and before any new model is run on the confirmation set
status: exploratory (confirmation set previously opened under lock v3); fixes the comparison in advance
question: Does changing only the starting weights reduce shared blind spots, for a CNN as well as a ViT, with enough events to tell?

models.vit_base: ImageNet supervised (existing), MAE, DINOv2; 3 seeds each (trained)
models.resnet50: ImageNet supervised a1_in1k (existing resnet50_5class), semi-weakly supervised fb_swsl_ig1b_ft_in1k (new), self-supervised DINO ResNet-50 (new); 3 seeds each; canonical CNN recipe

evaluation_set: EyePACS confirmation set (15,794 eyes, 7,897 patients), 25% eye-level referral as in lock v3, patient-cluster bootstrap (1,000)

outcomes.primary: co-miss ratio for referable disease by pair type
secondary: co-miss ratio for grade 3 or worse and for PDR

pair_types.same_architecture_different_init: reported for ViT-Base and ResNet50 separately and pooled
pair_types.different_architecture: pairs among ViT-Base supervised, ResNet50 supervised, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B3, RETFound
pair_types.new_init_vs_other_architecture: each new-initialisation model with each model of a different architecture

what_counts_as_a_signal.starting_weights_matter: same_architecture_different_init clearly below seed_siblings (interval of the difference excludes zero), separately for each architecture
what_counts_as_a_signal.architecture_matters_more: different_architecture clearly below same_architecture_different_init, before and after the strength adjustment

strength_adjustment: pair-level regression of log co-miss ratio on pair type with the pair's mean and gap in referable misses
decision_this_informs: whether paper 2 needs a pretraining arm, or should vary only architecture family and training data
